seasonality.pattern: Two documented sterling seasonal patterns fall inside these horizons and neither is fabricated. The first, named explicitly in the currency brief, is the April UK fiscal year-end, which lies outside both windows and is therefore not applied. The second and directly relevant one is the northern hemisphere heating season, which runs from October and falls inside the strategic horizon: UK gas demand is seasonally highest from October to March and European storage refill competes with Asian LNG buyers through the autumn. In a normal year this is a mild recurring pattern; in 2026 it interacts with a closed Strait of Hormuz through which roughly one-fifth of global LNG trade normally passes, which converts a seasonal pattern into a specific supply event and is why this dossier treats the gas price primarily as a dated fundamental rather than a seasonal effect. A third pattern applies at the far edge of the strategic horizon: year-end portfolio rebalancing and the 31 December dollar-funding turn, at which dealer balance-sheet compression reliably widens cross-currency basis. With the 3-month EUR/USD basis benign at roughly -16 to -20 basis points and the derived GBP/USD basis at about -12.5 basis points, that turn is a technical rather than a directional consideration this year, though London's role as a large dollar-borrowing centre makes UK institutions the natural stress point if it does bite. No other sterling seasonal pattern is asserted.
seasonality.relevance_window: The heating season is relevant from October 2026, inside the strategic horizon but outside the tactical one. The year-end funding turn is relevant at 31 December 2026, at the far edge of the strategic horizon. The April fiscal year-end falls outside both windows and is not applied.
seasonality.historical_magnitude: Not quantified. No dated historical study of sterling's seasonal amplitude was sourceable this cycle, so no magnitude is asserted rather than estimated. The observable current magnitude is UK gas running 18% to 21% above the Bank of England's own July conditioning assumption in the last week of August, which is a supply event rather than a seasonal one.
seasonality.current_alignment: Aligned with the bearish strategic thesis. The heating season arriving with the Strait of Hormuz effectively closed, European storage refill incomplete and NBP gas at 161-165 pence per therm against a BoE conditioning assumption of 136 means the seasonal demand increase lands on an already-tight balance, which sustains the terms-of-trade drag through the strategic window rather than relieving it.

assumptions: PHASE 6 VERIFICATION APPLIED. An adversarial fact-check run on 2026-09-01 confirmed 12 headline claims, flagged 7 and could not verify 2. Six corrections were made and are visible in the text: (a) 31 August 2026 was a UK bank holiday with gilt markets shut, so the 10-year is quoted at its 5.16% close of 28 August rather than a holiday print, the Bund at 3.32% and the spread at approximately 184 basis points rather than 189, and the since-June-2008 and since-1998 superlatives were withdrawn; (b) a working NBP gas figure of about 147 pence per therm at end-August and a +44.1% one-month move could not be reconciled with the dated 26-28 August prints of 160.50 to 165 pence and were withdrawn in favour of the 18% to 21% overshoot of the BoE conditioning assumption; (c) the DMO 2026-27 remit was corrected to the 23 April revision, which REDUCED the requirement to GBP 251.2 billion with GBP 246.2 billion of gilt sales, and the GBP 10.6 billion adjustment was corrected to negative; (d) UK Q2 GDP year-on-year was corrected from 1.1% to 1.2%; (e) the FTSE 100 was corrected from 10,743 (mid-August) to approximately 10,815 at the 28 August close, and the August PMI description from a board-wide beat to a beat on composite and services with manufacturing in line and lower; (f) the widely-repeated claim that Goldman Sachs and JPMorgan target 1.28 could not be corroborated and is flagged rather than relied on. Confidence was lowered on the affected factors: Factor 1 tactical 60 to 57, Factor 3 tactical 55 to 53, Factor 5 tactical 55 to 52 and strategic 68 to 63, Factor 8 tactical 62 to 58 and strategic 70 to 66. The weighted scores were recomputed accordingly, from -0.1542 to -0.1456 tactically and from -0.4300 to -0.4192 strategically; neither conviction level changed.

BEST AVAILABLE, FLAGGED: UK sovereign credit ratings. S&P AA and Fitch AA- are corroborated across sources, but the Moody's level is reported variously as Aa2 and Aa3 and no current outlook could be established from a dated primary source. The claim that all three agencies carry a negative footing is therefore presented as best available rather than established, and no analytical weight is placed on the outlook direction. Japanese CPI (headline 1.9%, core excluding fresh food 1.8%, from the 21 August 2026 release) was recorded as a cache gap in the primary research pass and filled during verification; it is likewise marked best available because it is a secondary retrieval.

COLLECTION FAILURES rather than genuine data gaps, to be fixed next cycle: a current UK 2-year gilt yield IS published and obtainable, so carrying a late-July level of about 4.35% is a collection miss; the Bank of England sterling effective exchange rate index IS published daily by the Bank in its statistical database, so its absence across two consecutive cycles is a collection miss; a UK 5-year sovereign CDS quote IS published on the same source used here for the gilt-Bund spread; and Japanese CPI is freely published monthly. These are distinguished in the text from the genuinely hard gaps - the 25-delta risk reversal, the cross-currency basis quotes, the 1-year implied-volatility percentile, the BIS REER percentile, and the Singapore macro series.

The pipeline data cache is treated as the source of truth for policy rates, FX spot levels and derived analytics (moving averages, realised volatility, ATR, performance, 52-week ranges, support and resistance zones), scheduled central bank decision dates, BIS real effective exchange rates and the point-in-time macro vintages. Web research supplies narrative, guidance, catalysts, citations and the figures the cache does not hold. Where the two disagree on a level, the cache is used and the discrepancy is noted.

Spot and derived analytics are as at the cache's price-store tail of 28 August 2026 (weekday bars only); series pulls run to 29 August 2026. The 31 August GBP/USD level of 1.3547 is quoted where it is the more current reference but the 1.35355 cache close is used for all derived calculations so that they reconcile with the downstream pair analysis.

The cached sovereign 10-year series (IRLTLT01) are MONTHLY and as at 1 June 2026 - approximately 92 days old, which breaches both the 30-day tactical and 60-day strategic freshness windows. The gilt level used is the 5.16% close of 28 August 2026 - the last traded level before the 31 August UK bank holiday, when gilt markets were shut - paired with a German Bund of 3.32% on 31 August, giving a spread of approximately 184 basis points. An earlier working set of 5.14% and 3.25% implying 189 basis points was corrected in verification and is recorded here; every other peer 10-year is quoted with its 1 June 2026 as-of date attached and must not be read as a live level.

The BIS real effective exchange rate is for the June 2026 period, approximately 63 days old and marginally outside the strategic freshness window. Its historical percentile of 70 is an explicit estimate: the cache carries the level and the one-year change only, not a full distribution.

The PPP deviation table is NOT a purchasing power parity fair value. No free PPP source was obtainable, so the table reports relative BIS REER standing - the percentage by which sterling's REER of 111.41 exceeds or falls short of each peer's - and the implied fair values are the spot rates that would equalise the two REER levels. This is a relative-valuation proxy and is labelled as such throughout.

The GBP/USD 1-year implied volatility percentile of 35 is a labelled estimate, not a quote. It is inferred from 60-day realised volatility of 5.41% sitting in the lower half of its own one-year range together with the contango shape of the term structure (5.544% at 43.6 days, 6.189% at 99.6, 6.578% at 190.6). No 1-year implied volatility history exists in the cache and none was sourceable free.

The 25-delta 1-month GBP/USD risk reversal is a documented gap. No reliably dated free quote could be sourced, so option skew is not assessed and no value is asserted. The same gap was recorded for EUR and CHF in this cycle.

The 3-month GBP/USD cross-currency basis of approximately -12.5 basis points is DERIVED, not quoted: it is inferred from the cache's GBP/USD futures-implied roll premium of 0.0 basis points annualised set against the +12.5 basis point policy differential. The 3-month EUR/USD basis of -16 to -20 basis points and 3-month term SOFR of about 3.62% are mid-May 2026 references, roughly 3.5 months old and flagged as stale. The 3-month JPY/USD basis is a documented gap.

The UK 2-year gilt yield of approximately 4.35% is from late July 2026 and is stale; it is used only to compute an indicative 2s10s of about +79 basis points, which is presented as indicative rather than precise.

The cached CFTC disaggregated tranche is 11 August 2026, 21 days before the valuation date and stale for a tactical read. The current headline non-commercial net of -44,500 contracts (28 August release, data to 25 August) is taken from research and cited. The two figures come from different CFTC report taxonomies - legacy non-commercial versus disaggregated leveraged funds and asset managers - and are not directly comparable; both are presented with their taxonomy stated.

Carry-to-volatility ratios are computed as the policy-rate differential in percentage points divided by 60-day realised volatility in percent, with the realised volatility read directly from the cache's derived files rather than estimated or recomputed, and never constructed from two USD legs. The basis is stated as carry divided by 60-day realised throughout.

Forward points for GBP/USD are derived rather than quoted: no free forward-points source was obtainable, so the 1-month, 3-month and 6-month outrights are computed from the cache's observed futures-implied roll premium of 0.0 basis points annualised and, alternatively, from the +12.5 basis point policy differential. Both derivations are shown and labelled.

Scheduled central bank decision dates come exclusively from the pipeline's calendar file and were never web-searched. The 4 February 2027 Bank of England Monetary Policy Report date is flagged as provisional in that file - published but not committed to - and is presented as provisional rather than firm.

The macro comparison table uses the point-in-time OECD and Eurostat vintages visible on the valuation date, except where a vintage lags by more than two quarters and a monthly research print is materially fresher, in which case the research print is used and the superseded vintage is named in the measure field. Japanese CPI and every Singapore macro cell are documented gaps, not estimates.

UK sovereign CDS spreads and a Citi Economic Surprise Index for the United Kingdom are documented gaps. The cache calendar's actual-versus-forecast record is used as the surprise substitute and the ratings outlooks are used as the sovereign-credit substitute.

The Bank of England sterling effective exchange rate index for August 2026 was not sourceable free, as was also the case in the previous cycle. The BIS REER is used as the trade-weighted measure in its place.
